To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ATR gene is alternatively spliced within the non-catalytic region of the mRNA transcript.
alternate splicing occurs within the mRNA transcript for the DNA damage response protein ATR, resulting in the expression of at least two forms of the protein.
the mRNA encoding the DNA damage checkpoint protein kinase ATR undergoes alternative splicing within the coding region of its non-catalytically active domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the ATR gene and its expression in human tissues, and has led to the identification of a novel splicing event within the ATR transcript.
the characterization of alternate ATR mRNA transcripts, and provides the first evidence that the non-catalytic region of the Atr protein undergoes alternate spicing.
the identification of factors that regulate the activity of the PIK-like kinase ATR.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ATR mRNA undergoes alternate spliced within the non-catalytic region.
the ATR transcript undergoes alternate spicing within the region of its non-catalylic domain.
the ATR gene is alternatively spliced in a tissue specific fashion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the human ATR gene undergoes alternate spicing within the region of its mRNA that encodes the large non-cataclytic domain of the ATR polypeptide.
the non-catalytic regions of PIK-like proteins may be functionally important, and may be regulated by alternate splicing.
alternate splicing of the ATR transcript may be a mechanism by which the cell controls the expression of a functional ATR protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PIK-like kinases, like many other kinases, are regulated at the level of transcription and mRNA processing.
the ATR gene encodes multiple isoforms of the protein, and that this is accomplished by alternate splicing.

alternate splicing of the ATR gene transcript may be of functional significance, and that the non-catalytic region of the ATRA protein may contain subdomains important for the regulation of its kinase activity and/or function.
